title: After the event: safe return, recovery and leading your community

say: After the event: safe return, recovery and leading your community.
This is the video for module three of Disaster Risk Management and Recovery.
Many injuries and illnesses happen after the water goes down or the fire is out. Electric shocks, collapsing walls, and diarrhoea from dirty water and spoiled food.

say: So recovery must start safely. Then you restart income, build back better, and lead your community.

say: Return only when SEMA, LEMA or local leaders say the area is safe, and in daylight.

panel.heading: Returning home safely
items: Return in daylight, when authorities say safe

say: Look from outside first. Cracks in walls, a sagging roof, a leaning building or a smell of gas mean do not enter.

say: Do not switch on electricity until a qualified electrician has checked the wiring, sockets and meter.

say: Wear closed shoes and gloves, because floodwater hides broken glass, nails and sewage. And take photos of all damage before you clean or throw anything away. You will need them for relief registration.

say: After a flood, treat all water as unsafe. Use your stored water first. Let cloudy water settle, and pour the clear part through a clean cloth.

panel.heading: Make water safe to drink
items: Bleach: plain, unscented, strength on label

say: Boiling is the safest method. Bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute, cool it, and store it covered.

panel.heading: Make water safe to drink
items: Bleach: plain, unscented, strength on label

say: Or use plain, unscented bleach whose label states its strength. For 5 to 9% bleach, add 2 drops per litre. If you cannot find the strength, do not guess. Boil instead.

panel.heading: Make water safe to drink
items: Bleach: plain, unscented, strength on label

say: For example, Zainab has 20 litres and 5% bleach. 20 times 2 is 40 drops. She waits at least 30 minutes. For her baby she chooses boiled water.

panel.heading: Make water safe to drink
items: Bleach: plain, unscented, strength on label

say: Never mix bleach with ammonia, acids or other cleaning products. It can release toxic gases. Keep it out of children's reach.

say: Throw away any food that touched floodwater, unless it is in a sealed, undamaged tin. Wash and disinfect pots and plates before use.
Cholera often follows floods. If anyone has sudden watery diarrhoea or vomiting, start oral rehydration salts mixed exactly as the sachet says, and go to the nearest health centre at once.
And sleep under a treated mosquito net.

say: Recovery means restarting income. Funmi lost stock worth about 180,000 naira. She has 60,000 naira in savings and 100,000 due from her ajo group next month.

card.title: Funmi's recovery budget
card.note: Naira prices are approximate, for illustration.

say: She needs 150,000 naira to restock, 35,000 for the freezer, and 45,000 for shelves to raise her stock.

card.title: Funmi's recovery budget
card.note: Naira prices are approximate, for illustration.

say: That is 230,000 naira, so her gap is 70,000. She restocks fast-moving goods first so cash flows, asks a supplier for 2 weeks' credit, and delays the freezer.
And she never pays anyone to add her name to a relief list. Real registration never asks for a fee, your PIN or OTP.

say: The common mistake is to rebuild exactly as before: stock on the floor, low sockets, papers in the drawer.

panel.heading: Repair is the cheapest moment
left: Sockets at the same low height

say: Instead, mark the highest water level on a wall and store goods above it. Ask an electrician to raise sockets. Most of these choices cost little extra when done during repair. If you rent, agree changes with your landlord in writing first.

panel.heading: Repair is the cheapest moment

say: You do not need a title to lead. For example, Hauwa in Lokoja showed her women's group the flood mark on the old mosque wall.

say: Women audited their homes. The average was 13 of 40, or 33 percent.

say: The CDA agreed to two drain-clearing days, and she wrote to the LGA with a specific request.

say: After 90 days, her street averaged 24 of 40, or 60 percent. Clear, measurable requests and results win more support.

panel.rule: A clear request names who, what, how many and when.

say: To remember. Return safely and keep the power off until it is checked. Make water safe, and discard flooded food.
Support people with Look, Listen, Link. Restart income first, build back better, and lead with local evidence.

panel.heading: Remember
